findings.reason: without a multi-engine golden, §5 can pass its gate with a shape §7 and §14 then build against, which freezes the guess §14's own rationale exists to prevent.
findings.text: §5's mechanism defines how a pool document aggregates several engines (§5 lines 211-221: counts and capacities sum, per-request figures weighted by running count, an `engines` array carries each engine's own reading), and §14 is declared to depend on exactly that shape ("it reads the per-pool documents and per-engine figures they publish", §11 line 602), yet every §5 done-when bullet exercises a single-engine document: bullet 1 is "one engine's fixture readings" (line 234) and bullet 2 is "a two-pool fixture writes two pool documents" (line 238), i.e. two pools of one engine each, with the negative control (line 250) likewise a one-engine-per-pool case. Nothing gates the aggregation branch, so a node can ship the per-pool split and pass all five bullets while the summed counts, the weighted per-request figures and the `engines` array — the shape §7's two-engine pool and §14 consume — were never verified
